skill.name: conventions
skill.description: Use project coding conventions to guide code writing, review, refactoring, and style decisions.
skill.summary: Loads project coding conventions for consistent code work.
skill.author: Clouder0

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt file. Manual review found a read-only coding conventions skill with no executable code, network behavior, secret handling, or prompt-injection attempt.

content.value_statement: Codebases drift when contributors apply different style choices. This skill loads project conventions so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can follow shared standards.
actual_capabilities: Loads coding conventions before writing new code.
Applies style guidance during code reviews.
Supports refactoring decisions with project standards.
Points the assistant to the conventions file at memory/knowledge/codebase/conventions.json.
Covers naming, file organization, error handling, testing, and documentation standards.
limitations: It depends on the referenced conventions file being available.
It does not enforce rules automatically in a build system.
It does not include executable validation scripts.
It only requests read access for convention context.

use_cases.title: Standardize New Features
use_cases.description: Apply repository naming, file layout, and testing expectations before generating new code.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check proposed changes against shared style, error handling, documentation, and test conventions.

use_cases.title: Guide Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Keep refactors aligned with existing project standards while improving structure or readability.

prompt_templates.title: Load Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the project coding conventions and summarize the rules I should follow for this task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for understanding the active project standards.

prompt_templates.title: Write With Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project coding conventions while implementing this change. Call out any convention that affects your approach.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before writing a new feature or small fix.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change against the project coding conventions. Focus on naming, file organization, tests, errors, and documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this refactor using the project coding conventions. Identify standards that should shape the file layout, tests, and error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for multi-file maintenance work.

output_examples.input: Review a new service module for convention fit.
output: Naming follows the repository pattern for service classes.
The file belongs with related domain services, not shared utilities.
Add a focused unit test for the documented error path.

output_examples.input: Plan a refactor before editing a feature area.
output: Keep public function names stable unless the convention requires a rename.
Move helper logic near the feature owner module.
Update documentation if the user-facing behavior changes.

best_practices: Load the conventions before generating or reviewing code.
Ask for specific convention checks when reviewing a diff.
Update the referenced conventions file when project standards change.
anti_patterns: Using the skill without the conventions file available.
Treating suggestions as a substitute for tests or linters.
Applying conventions from another repository without checking local rules.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells the assistant to load project coding conventions before code writing, review, refactoring, or style decisions.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prompt-only and requests read access for convention context.

faq.question: What convention areas are covered?
faq.answer: It covers naming, file organization, error handling, testing, and documentation standards.

faq.question: Can it enforce conventions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides assistant behavior but does not replace linters, tests, or build checks.

faq.question: What file does it reference?
faq.answer: It references memory/knowledge/codebase/conventions.json as the source for project conventions.
